title: Godot project crashes if Mesh.GetFaces() called too many times in a single update
body:
### Tested versions

Very slightly tested in 4.4-stable (just to the extent of "confirmed the crash happens when the project that has the issue in 4.4.1, is tested in 4.4")
Tested more extensively in 4.4.1-stable

### System information

Godot v4.4.1.stable.mono - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated AMD Radeon Graphics (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.21001.9024) - AMD Ryzen Z1 Extreme (16 threads)

### Issue description

[font.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20537525/font.zip)

NOTE: I've made references to the C# functions in the description here. However, I have confirmed the issue occurs even when using GDScript, and have updated the report to include a GDScript MRP.

This is the GLB file I am running into the issue with, in case it is a fault with the file. However I will note this issue has occured across several variations of this file. The file consists of multiple meshes that are intended to work as a font, one for each supported character (33 through 126 in the ASCII character set).

During loading, I instantiate a copy of this via GD.Load<PackedScene>.Instantiate<Node3D>. I then iterate through the children (which are all MeshInstance3Ds). GetFaces() is called on each MeshInstance3D's mesh during this iteration. In my original project, even a single call to this on each MeshInstance3D is enough to trigger the crash (initially three calls were made, but I tidied up the code to reduce the calls to it, and the issue persisted); while on a "minimum case" reproduction, it only occurred if GetFaces was called multiple times on each instance within a single update loop.

The result of this is that, either at the end of the update cycle or the start of the next one, the game freezes. It does not respond to input (including Alt+F4 or clicking the X to close it), and Windows detects it as not responding. Through the debugger in Visual Studio, or from writing data to files after the GetFaces() calls, I can confirm that GetFaces() doesn't _immediately_ cause the crash. However, if all calls to GetFaces() are removed (or even reduced in quantity), the crash no longer occurs. Removing everything _except_ the GetFaces() calls, had no effect on the crashes.

On further testing, I have discovered that this crash does not happen when using the Compatibility renderer. It happens on the Forward+ and Mobile renderers.

Summary:
- This happens with Forward+ and Mobile renderers; it does not happen with Compatibility renderer.
- Removing everything except the GetFaces calls in the relevant loops does **not** prevent the crash.
- Removing the GetFaces calls (while keeping everything else; including if the same data is obtained from another source eg. from saving it to a file on a previous run) **does** prevent the crash.
- Happens (at least on 4.4.1) in both C# and GDScript

### Steps to reproduce

This is mixed in with the description; see above. Or see the MRP below.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[GodotGetFacesBug_GDscript.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20573226/GodotGetFacesBug_GDscript.zip)
(Also includes C# version of the script)
